before.problem:
A small business collected data on the number of hours of telephone usage and the total amount (in hundreds of dollars) of the company's weekly operating expenses. This data is shown below.   

| Hours $(x)$ | **$2$** | **$2.4$** | **$2.8$** | **$3.2$** | **$3.6$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Expenses $(y)$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ | $8$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the company's weekly operating expenses if the telephone is used for a total of $4$ hours per week, assuming the trend continues?

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}40.8 & -14 \\ -14 & 5\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}30 \\ 88\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*

Hint: You can use the fact that (XTX)−1=18[40.8−14−145],XTy=[3088], where X is the corresponding design matrix and y is the observation vector.

a
$850
b
$900
c
$1050
d
$875
e

decision.explanation: The regression coefficients are β₀=(40.8·30−14·88)/8=−1 and β₁=(−14·30+5·88)/8=2.5. Thus y=−1+2.5x, and at x=4, y=9 hundreds of dollars, or $900.

after.problem:
A small business collected data on the number of hours of telephone usage and the total amount (in hundreds of dollars) of the company's weekly operating expenses. This data is shown below.   

| Hours $(x)$ | **$2$** | **$2.4$** | **$2.8$** | **$3.2$** | **$3.6$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Expenses $(y)$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ | $8$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the company's weekly operating expenses if the telephone is used for a total of $4$ hours per week, assuming the trend continues?

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}40.8 & -14 \\ -14 & 5\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}30 \\ 88\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2.4 \\ 1 & 2.8 \\ 1 & 3.2 \\ 1 & 3.6\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 6 \\ 7 \\ 8\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}40.8 & -14 \\ -14 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}30 \\ 88\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2.5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=-1+2.5x.$

Finally, to predict the amount of the company's weekly operating expenses if the telephone is used for a total of $4$ hours, we substitute $x=4$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-1+2.5(4) \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

So, according to the model, the company's weekly operating expenses will be $$900.$ 

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=4$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
A store collected data about its profits (in thousands of dollars) for the first five months since opening. This data is shown below.

| Month $(x)$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Profit $(y)$ | $8.3$ | $5.1$ | $10.9$ | $10.7$ | $9.5$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the profit in the $6$th month, assuming that the trend continues?

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}44.5 \\ 141.5\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}8.3 \\ 5.1 \\ 10.9 \\ 10.7 \\ 9.5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}44.5 \\ 141.5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6.5 \\ 0.8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=6.5+0.8x.$

Finally, to predict the profit in the $6$th month, we substitute $x=6$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =6.5+0.8(6) \\  & =11.3\end{aligned}
$$

So, according to the model, the profit in the $6$th month will be $$11\,300.$

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=6$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.

after.problem:
A store collected data about its profits (in thousands of dollars) for the year's first five months. This data is shown below.

| Month $(x)$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Profit $(y)$ | $12$ | $15$ | $16$ | $15$ | $20$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above. According to the model, what will be the profit in the $6$th month, assuming the trend continues?

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}78 \\ 250\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}12 \\ 15 \\ 16 \\ 15 \\ 20\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}11 & -3 \\ -3 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}78 \\ 250\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10.8 \\ 1.6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=10.8+1.6x.$ 

Finally, to predict the profit in the $6$th month, we substitute $x=6$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =10.8+1.6(6) \\  & =20.4\end{aligned}
$$

So, according to the model, the profit in the $6$th month will be $$20\,400.$

**Note**: Since we're extrapolating ($x=6$ is not within the range of the original set of $x$-values), our result *may* be unreliable.

decision.explanation: The least-squares coefficients are β₀=(6·6−2·32)/10=−2.8 and β₁=(−2·6+32)/10=2. Therefore the best-fit line is y=−2.8+2x, option d.

| $y$ | $-3$ | $-1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $5$ |

Find the line of the form $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x$ that best fits the data above.

*Hint: You can use the fact that*

$$
({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}=\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{X}^{T}y=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 32\end{aligned}],
$$

*where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector.*
after.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the line that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$

Substituting the given values of $({X}^{T}X)^{-1}$ and ${X}^{T}y$ into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\beta } & =({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}\,y \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ 32\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2.8 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the line $y=-2.8+2x.$
